title: Inertia of a body with its own mark in a weakly pinned field of oscillator cells

key_results.statement: Ring and cubic torus, every $L$, $M\to\infty$ first, every isolated state (6.4), $P$ near 0: $E_{k,\sigma}(P)=E_f+\sigma\sqrt{M_k^2\bar F^2+\tau^2\sin^2P}+E^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}(P)+O(\delta F^3)$, even in $P$, with $\bar F=F_0+F_2w_0$; for a non-isolated upper branch under (U) these are formal coefficients.

$E^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}(P)=-M_k^2\langle\!\langle\cos^2\vartheta/(E+\sigma[\omega(P-Q)-\omega(P)])+\sin^2\vartheta/(E-\sigma[\omega(P-Q)+\omega(P)])\rangle\!\rangle$, $\vartheta=\frac12[\theta(P)+\theta(P-Q)]$, a spectral sum over one- and two-quantum field states (6.1).

Both graphs, $\ell^2\ge3/(4D)$, $L\to\infty$, $\delta F\to0$: $(k,\sigma)$ has a gap to every sector of field excitations iff $b_k=\min_q[\Omega_q-\omega_k(q_1)]>\sigma\varepsilon_k$; lower branch iff $\varepsilon_k>\varepsilon_-(r)$ with $\varepsilon_-=0$ for $r\le1$ ($\tau^2\le2\varepsilon_kc_0$ suffices); upper branch iff $\varepsilon_k<\varepsilon_+(r)\le m_h/2$ (light levels only; $(2\varepsilon_k/m_h)^2+r^2<1$ suffices); otherwise the upper-branch coefficients are formal, finite under (U).

$C^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}=\sigma M_k\bar F$ for every $\tau$; $C^{\rm mark}_{k,\sigma}=E^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}(0)=-M_k^2(F_1^2G_0/2+2F_2^2J_2)(1+\delta_C)$, $\delta_C=\tau^2\langle\!\langle\sin^2Q/[E^2(E-2\sigma\varepsilon_k)]\rangle\!\rangle/\langle\!\langle1/E\rangle\!\rangle+O(\tau^4)$; the held mark is strictly negative.

Both graphs, every $L,\ell$, $\tau>0$, isolated states: $I^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}=C^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}/\tau^2$ for every $r$; $I^{\rm mark}_{k,\sigma}=-\varepsilon_k^2E^{(2)\prime\prime}_{k,\sigma}(0)/\tau^4$; a single $v$ on the set $\mathcal S$ of isolated states exists iff $\rho_{k,\sigma}=\tau^2I^{\rm mark}/C^{\rm mark}=1$ on $\mathcal S$, and then $v=\tau$.

Ring, $L\gg\ell$, under (6.4) (formal for $\sigma=+1$, which is not isolated where $\delta_\ell\ll1$), up to relative $O(\delta_\ell)$: $C^{\rm mark}=-\frac{M_k^2\ell}{4c_0^2}(F_1^2+\frac{F_2^2}{2c_0})$, $\zeta=F_2^2/2c_0$, $E^{(2)\prime\prime}(0)=-\frac{2\tau^2}{\varepsilon_k^2}C^{\rm mark}[1-\frac{r^2}{2}-\sigma\varepsilon_kR]$, with $R=O(\ln^2\ell/c_0\ell)$.

Ring, $L\gg\ell$, every (G2) grip, every $r>0$, isolated lower branches: $\rho_{k,-}=2-r^2+2\varepsilon_kR+O(\delta_\ell)$; at leading order in $1/\ell$ (fixed $\varepsilon_k/c_0$, where $\mathcal S$ has only lower branches) $I^{\rm mark}_{k,-}=(2-r^2)C^{\rm mark}_{k,-}/\tau^2$, so for nonempty $\mathcal S$ one $v$ for $I^{(1)}$ and $I^{\rm mark}$ on $\mathcal S$ exists iff $r=1$, with $v=\tau=c_0$; first difference $(1-r^2)C^{\rm mark}/\tau^2$.

Both graphs, every $L,\ell$, isolated lower branch with $\varepsilon_k\gg c_0$, $\varepsilon_k^2\gg\tau^2(1+r^2)$: $\rho_{k,-}=\rho^{\rm e}_k+2\varepsilon_kR[1+O((c_0^2+\tau^2(1+r^2))/\varepsilon_k^2)]$ with $\rho^{\rm e}_k=O(1+r^2)$; in the heavy regime ($\varepsilon_kR\gg1+r^2$, $\tau^2\ll\varepsilon_kc_0$) $I^{\rm mark}_{k,-}=I^{(1)}_{k,-}Y_k$ and $\rho_{k,-}=2\varepsilon_kR\gg1$, so no single $v$ at any $r$ ($r=1$ included) and finite $\ell$, and $\rho_{k,-}$ grows with the level.

Both graphs, every $L,\ell,r$, isolated states, second order in $\delta F$ with $F_1,F_2$ counted alike, weights (2.8): $E''\Delta W=\frac{\tau^2F_1\Delta\phi}{F_0}[1-F_2w_0/F_0-2\sigma M_kF_2G_0]$, the same on $\mathcal S$ (at least two states) iff $F_2=0$; for $F_2=0$ the first level dependence comes from $I^{\rm mark}$ via (6.12): on the ring at leading order in $1/\ell$ it vanishes only at $r=\sqrt2$, on the cubic torus it differs between any two isolated lower levels at the computed points.

Grips of fixed shape through relative order $\beta^2$, weights (2.8), isolated states: $E''\Delta W=\frac{\tau^2F_1\Delta\phi}{F_0}[1-F_2w_0/F_0-2\sigma M_kF_2G_0-I^{\rm mark}/I^{(1)}]$; on the ring at leading order in $1/\ell$, with at least two isolated levels, the same on $\mathcal S$ iff $(2-r^2)F_1^2=4F_0F_2$ (square grip iff $r=1$, linear grip only at $r=\sqrt2$); in the heavy regime the lower-branch bracket is quadratic in $M_k$ with leading coefficient $-F_1^2G_0R_1\ne0$, so no grip for three levels and exactly one, $F_0F_2/F_1^2=R_1(\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_b)/2$, for two.

Both graphs, isolated states: with $E^{(2)}=-M_k^2(F_1^2S_1+F_2^2S_2)$ and $\xi=F_2^2/(c_0F_1^2)$, $\rho_{k,\sigma}=(S_1\rho_1+\xi c_0S_2\rho_2)/(S_1+\xi c_0S_2)$ and $\rho_{k,\sigma}=1$ iff $S_1(\rho_1-1)+\xi c_0S_2(\rho_2-1)=0$; for $S_1,S_2>0$ a grip achieves this iff $\rho_1=1$ ($\xi=0$; every $\xi$ if also $\rho_2=1$) or $(\rho_1-1)(\rho_2-1)<0$ (one $\xi^*>0$), none if $\rho_2=1\ne\rho_1$; the bracket of (6.12) is $1-F_2w_0/F_0-\sigma(\varepsilon_kF_1^2G_0/F_0^2)(2y-t_{k,\sigma})$ with $y=F_0F_2/F_1^2$.

Cubic torus, every (G2) grip, isolated states: negative for the class by members with margins at $r=1$ (a level at $\varepsilon_k=4c_0$ has $\rho_{k,-}\ge1.40$ for every grip at $\ell=8$ and $32$; two levels at $1.2c_0$ and $2c_0$ need different $\xi^*$; light levels have $\rho<1$ on both branches); numerical finding at the grid points ($L=8\ell$, $\ell=8,32$, $r\in[0.1,3]$, $\varepsilon_k/c_0\in[0.1,64]$): one $v$ exists exactly when $\mathcal S$ is the lower branch of a single level in the window (about $[0.912,2.612)c_0$ at $r=1$) with $\xi=\xi^*_{k,-}$, which requires $r>1$; then $v=\tau$.

Cubic torus, isolated states without light levels, relative order $\beta^2$, weights (2.8): $E''\Delta W$ is the same on $\mathcal S$ iff $\sigma\varepsilon_k(2y-t_{k,\sigma})$ is (two lower levels need $y=y_{ab}$, three need $(\varepsilon_k,\varphi(\varepsilon_k))$ collinear); negative member at $r=1$: levels $(1,2,3)c_0$ give $y_{12}=0.563\ne y_{23}=0.804$; at the grid points two lower levels admit exactly one grip, three or more none where $\varphi$ is discretely convex, the linear grip fails, and the square grip is not singled out.

open_issues: Cubic torus: the findings of (6.14) and (6.15) hold at the grid points of Step 10 (L = 64, ℓ = 8 and L = 256, ℓ = 32; r in [0.1, 3]; ε_k/c_0 in [0.1, 64]; lower branch at least 0.2 m_h above its threshold; light levels at the points of Part F); nothing is claimed between grid points, for r > 3, closer to the lower threshold, or in the limit ℓ → ∞; near the threshold the values still change with ℓ.
Light levels: item 3 is not evaluated for descriptions with a light level, and item 2 only at the points of Part F (ℓ = 8).
Upper branch outside the isolated set: only its formal coefficients are given; its behaviour beyond second order (decay into the continuum) is not computed.
The weight of the moving body is taken from (2.8) without corrections in τ; (6.11) and (6.12) rest on this.
On the ring the expansion parameter grows like ℓ, so (6.8)–(6.12) need δF to shrink as ℓ grows; the regime M_k F_1² G_0 ∼ F_0 is open.

consistency_checks.check: Held limit τ→0: E^(2)(0) equals the second-order part of the mark cost in (2.6)
Bare body δF=0, F0=1: E''(0)=στ²/M_k as in (6.7) of 04-ilang-time/06-inertia-internal-energy
